findings: The one-bit pair 0000000000000000 / 8000000000000000 is not compared when prefixes 00,01,02,80 are occupied: positions differ by three and search considers only adjacent occupied positions. This proves candidate-rule incompleteness independently of image decoding.

Exhaustive unordered pairs of all 256 occupied first-byte buckets, with remaining 56 bits identical, show omitted eligible pairs at every configured image/video threshold. These counts concern synthetic hash pairs, not measured real-world image recall.

A candidate pair omitted by this rule could still share a final group through another anchor or group-ID merging; the counterexample proves missing direct comparisons, not universal final-group separation.
